info.title: Devias API
info.description: Metadata-driven operations platform: records, metadata, modules, workflows and a change feed.

Id.description: Stable identifier shared by module source and workspace metadata

blockId.description: The block's id: core.fields (the record's fields; config.fieldIds lists fields by id or API name, default all), core.related_records (records whose relation points at this one; config.objectId, config.fieldId (its relation field), optional config.limit), core.activity (history), or a record block an installed module declares (e.g. acme.person-summary). list_blocks lists them all with their config.

post.description: Moves several nav items at once, so a reorder is one change. A module’s items are moved as the workspace’s choice and survive module updates.

requestBody.description: The new parent and position of each item moved

post.description: Drops the workspace’s overrides of a module’s nav item, so it shows as the module defines it.
Clears the workspace’s overrides of every nav item, so the sidebar is as the modules and the studio define it. Items the workspace created are kept.

requestBody.description: Query IR; the path object wins over the body

post.description: Counts and measures (sum, average, min, max) over the records that match, per group of one field or in total. Select fields list every option, in order.

requestBody.description: What to group by and measure; the filter is the query filter

200.description: Groups with their count and measures, and the totals

get.summary: Get a record with the labels of its relations
get.description: The record, and for each relation field the record it points at, so a reader can say who it is.

200.description: The record and the records its relations point at

post.summary: Create or update a record by a unique field
post.description: Finds the record whose unique field has the given value: updates it with `values`, or creates one with `values` and the match. The field must be unique.

requestBody.description: The unique field to match on, and the values

200.description: The record, and whether it was created

requestBody.description: Up to 500 operations in one transaction

200.description: What was created, updated and deleted

post.summary: Import records from the rows of a file
post.description: Reads the cells as text by the rules of the import (numbers, dates, options, related records by name), validates every row, writes the valid ones and reports the rest by row. `dryRun` writes nothing. At most 500 rows per call: send a bigger file in several.

requestBody.description: The columns, the rows as text and how to read them

200.description: How many were created, updated and skipped, and the problems by row

get.description: Changes, newest first. Page with `nextCursor`.
Newest first. Page with `nextCursor`; `total` is how many the record has.

post.summary: Add a note to a record

requestBody.description: The note: a title and an optional body

patch.description: Authors can edit their own notes; owners and admins any.

requestBody.description: The title and/or the body to change

delete.description: Authors can remove their own notes; owners and admins any.

get.description: Newest change first, without their text; page with `nextCursor`. `search` matches the title and the text, `mentions` keeps the documents that mention a record or another document (`record:<object>/<id>`, `document:<id>`), `ids` picks some by id.

post.description: A title and, optionally, the text as `markdown` (or as an editor document in `body`). Mention a record or a document with a link, `[Label](record:<object>/<id>)` or `[Label](document:<id>)`.

requestBody.description: The document: a title and, optionally, its text

get.description: The whole document: its text as an editor document (`body`) and as Markdown, and its `version`.

patch.description: Sends only what changes. A new `body` or `markdown` replaces the whole text. With `expectedVersion`, a document that changed since is a `CONFLICT`; without it the change overwrites.

delete.description: The document stops being listed, readable and linked.

post.description: Adds Markdown after the last block, atomically: nothing needs reading first, and a person typing meanwhile loses nothing.

200.description: The document with the text added

get.description: When it was made, who edited it and the comments written on it, newest first; page with `nextCursor`.

post.description: Adds a comment as Markdown; mention with `[Label](record:<object>/<id>)` or `[Name](member:<userId>)`. Give `anchor.quote`, text of the document, to put it on that text (the studio underlines it and shows the comment beside it); give `parent`, the id of a top-level comment, to reply to its thread. A comment does not change the document or its version.

requestBody.description: The comment: its text, and optionally the text it is on or the comment it replies to

get.summary: List the comments of a document
get.description: Threads: each a top-level comment (with the text it is on, if any, and whether it is resolved) and its replies, oldest first. `status` is `open` (default), `resolved` or `all`.

patch.description: Send `resolved: true` to resolve a top-level comment (and so its thread) or `false` to reopen it; send `markdown` to change the text, which only its author or an admin may do.

delete.description: Only its author or an admin may. Deleting a top-level comment deletes its replies.

get.description: Most recently changed first, without their text; page with `nextCursor`. `assignee` is `me`, `unassigned`, `agents`, `people`, `user:<id>` or `agent:<id>`; `scope` is `open` or `closed`; `due` is `overdue`, `today`, `week` or `none`; `parent` keeps the subtasks of a task (or `none` for top-level tasks); `mentions` keeps the tasks that mention or are about a record, a document or a task (`record:<object>/<id>`, `document:<id>`, `task:<id>`); `search` matches the title and the description.

post.description: A title and, optionally, the description as `markdown` (or as an editor document in `body`), `priority`, `dueDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), an `assignee` (`user:<id>`, `agent:<id>`), a `parent` task and what it is `about` (`record:<object>/<id>`, `document:<id>`). Mention a record, a document, a task or a member with a link: `[Label](record:<object>/<id>)`, `[Label](document:<id>)`, `[Label](task:<id>)`, `[Name](member:<userId>)`. The same `key` twice returns the first task instead of making another.

requestBody.description: The task: a title and, optionally, its description, assignee and links

get.description: Open, overdue, due today and this week, in review, the caller’s own and by status.
The whole task: its description as an editor document (`body`) and as Markdown, what it mentions and is about, its subtask counts and its `version`.

patch.description: Sends only what changes. A new `body` or `markdown` replaces the whole description. With `expectedVersion`, a task that changed since is a `CONFLICT`; without it the change overwrites.  Moving a task to `done` or `canceled` closes it; any other status reopens it.

delete.description: The task and its subtasks stop being listed, readable and linked.

get.description: Comments, changes and agent runs of one task, newest first; page with `nextCursor`.

post.summary: Stop an agent working on a task
post.description: Cancels the run in progress, declines what it proposed and marks the task as failed until someone retries it.
Puts a failed or stopped task back in the agent’s queue.
Adds a comment to the task’s timeline as Markdown; mention with `[Label](record:<object>/<id>)` or `[Name](member:<userId>)`. A comment does not change the task’s version.

201.description: The comment, as a timeline entry

200.description: Every workflow of the workspace, oldest first

post.description: Owners and admins only. The trigger and steps are checked against the workspace metadata: objects, fields, filters and functions must exist.

patch.description: Sends only what changes. A new trigger, or enabling the workflow, starts it from now: events that happened in between are not replayed.

get.description: Newest first. Page with `nextCursor`.

How the workspace’s workflows have run: runs per day (succeeded and failed) over the last `days` days counted in `tz`, and for every workflow that has run, its runs and failures in that period and how its latest run ended.

200.description: Runs per day and per workflow

post.description: Runs the steps right away and returns the run. When the trigger names an object, `recordId` picks the record; the caller must be able to read it. The steps run as the workflow actor.
Runs the workflow again with the trigger of an earlier run (its record or module event), and returns the new run, which names the one it retries in `trigger.retryOf`.

get.summary: List the runs of a task
get.description: The attempts an agent made at the task, newest first: status, summary and error.
The caller’s notifications, newest first. `unread=true` keeps the unread ones; page with `nextCursor`.

post.description: Notify members: everyone (`to.all`), roles (`to.roles`), people by user id (`to.users`) or the caller (`to.me`). `target` says where it leads; a repeated `key` replaces the unread notification instead of adding one.

requestBody.description: The notification and who receives it

201.description: How many people it reached, and how many notifications were created or replaced

requestBody.description: The manifest to apply, optionally pinned to a reviewed plan

get.description: The manifest of every module registered on this server, installed in the workspace or not.
The workspace's connections and the caller's own, and the providers installed modules offer. Credentials never come back; `hints` carries masked previews.

post.description: Store an API key connection, encrypted, and test it against the outside service: the returned `status` is `connected` or `auth_failed` (see `lastError`). A person's own connection needs `module.connect`; a workspace one, owners and admins. OAuth providers connect through `connections.authorize`.

requestBody.description: The module, its provider and the values

patch.description: Replace some of its values, or its label; the connection is tested again.

post.description: The OAuth provider's consent page for the caller to open. Once they agree, the provider sends them to the server's callback, which stores the connection and sends them back to `returnTo`.

requestBody.description: The module and its OAuth provider

get.description: What is in effect for each variable the module declares, and where it comes from: this workspace, the server, the default, or nowhere. Secret values never come back.

patch.description: Owners and admins only. Sets this workspace's values of the module's workspace variables (an empty string goes back to the default); server variables are set in the server's environment.

get.description: Events the module delivered through its webhook, newest first. Page with `nextCursor`.
Background jobs of installed modules, newest first. Page with `nextCursor`.

post.description: Owners and admins only. A failed job goes back to pending, due now, with its attempts reset.

201.description: The new key; `key` is shown only once

200.description: Members with their role, oldest first

delete.description: They lose access to the workspace at once. Records they created stay.

post.description: They join with the given role when they accept, after signing up with this email if they have no account. Invitations expire after 48 hours.

get.description: The agents of this workspace with their tools; archived ones only when asked for.

201.description: The new agent (owners and admins only)

get.description: One agent's conversations started, replies given and tokens used (input and output) per day over the last `days` days counted in `tz`.

200.description: The agent's activity per day (owners and admins only)

get.description: How many conversations each agent has had (everyone's) and the tokens they used, for every agent including archived ones.

200.description: Usage per agent (owners and admins only)
text/event-stream. First `event: ready` with `{"sequence"}`, then events after `after` (or `Last-Event-ID`), then live events; each has `id: <sequence>` and `event: <type>`.

post.description: The URL a module's connection shows as `webhookUrl`. The signature is checked with that connection's webhook secret; the body is stored as the event payload. Unknown tokens answer 404, failed checks 400. Not for clients.

get.description: The redirect URI to register with an OAuth provider. It checks the state, exchanges the code, stores the connection and sends the person back to the studio. Not for clients.

200.description: How it went, for a window that closes itself

302.description: Back to the studio page the consent started from

get.description: The image the module declares as its `logo`, served from its package. Public. 404 when the module is unknown or declares none. Not for clients to build: the studio shows it where a module is listed.

304.description: Unchanged since the ETag the request sent

200.description: Whether the agent is configured, its model and the tools this user can use
This user's conversations, most recent first
The conversation with its messages and the active turn

Send a message and stream the turn. text/event-stream of ChatEvent frames: `event: <type>`, `data: <ChatEvent JSON>`; heartbeats are comment lines. The stream ends with `paused` (approval needed) or `done`.

Approve or reject a pending tool call and stream the rest of the turn. text/event-stream of ChatEvent frames: `event: <type>`, `data: <ChatEvent JSON>`; heartbeats are comment lines. The stream ends with `paused` (approval needed) or `done`.
The cancelled turn, or null when nothing was running
